methods.name: workdown.export
methods.summary: Export a Jira issue as the Workdown document an Exchange would share
methods.description: Read-only. Reads one issue as the caller, checks it against the named profile, and returns its Workdown document. Never stores or publishes anything. The document contains only the profile's allowlisted fields; nothing else on the issue is ever included. An optional field that is empty or not configured is omitted. Start date is found by its stable semantic identity, never by display name or a fixed field ID, so equivalent issues on different sites produce the same document. The caller must be able to read the issue. An issue that does not exist and one the caller cannot read produce the same forbidden error. An issue the caller can read but that the profile forbids sharing, such as one with issue-level security, produces issue-ineligible; it is returned only to a caller who can already read the issue and never discloses restricted content. If eligibility cannot be determined, the export fails with eligibility-undetermined; uncertainty is never permission. App-level access never authorizes disclosure. An issue that does not satisfy the profile produces profile-mismatch. A field that cannot be resolved to exactly one supported field produces field-unresolved. A field or value that cannot be read produces field-unreadable. The document includes a summary of each eligible direct child of the Epic, read through Jira's system parent relationship as the caller. Completed children are included. Grandchildren, subtasks of children, linked issues and the legacy Epic Link are never included. Children are ordered by immutable issue ID in lexical order, so the same content produces the same bytes regardless of how Jira ordered or paged its results. A child summary contains only identity, title, link, type, status and resolution; it has no description, comments or modification time. Children the caller cannot read, and children with issue-level security, are omitted silently, as Jira itself omits them from the caller's results: the document, errors and logs reveal no identity, title, count or reason for them. An Epic with no eligible children produces a document without a Children section. The export reads every page of children. If the listing cannot be read completely, the export fails with children-unreadable; a smaller snapshot is never returned and no child count is invented. A failed export never returns a partial document. Provisional application limits are 262144 UTF-8 bytes for the complete canonical document and 100 eligible direct children. Equality is allowed. Exceeding these limits produces Document too large (-32008) or Too many children (-32009), respectively; neither error is retryable without a source-content change. Excluded children do not count toward the child limit. Limit failures include no document, source values, counts, or diagnostics. Identical content on retry produces identical canonical bytes for direct comparison. Invalid required values fail the whole candidate with a sanitized error.

methods.name: exchange.start
methods.summary: Start sharing an Epic over an active outbound Peer Connection
methods.description: Mutation. Authenticate the caller within the source installation and independently verify current Project Admin authority for the Epic's project at the business boundary. Read and generate through the same caller-scoped eligibility and disclosure behavior as workdown.export. Require an active outbound Connection; pending, revoked, reverse-direction, unknown, or unavailable Connections fail without revealing their state. No destination project, Epic, or per-Exchange destination approval is accepted or required. In ticket 20 only the fixed development-only loopback Connection is available. Resolve the issue key or ID to stable source identity. The pair of Connection and stable Subject identity identifies one Exchange and one document: repeating start never creates another Exchange. Each invocation attempts immediate generation and delivery, including when the Exchange already exists. Allocate a sequence only for changed canonical Workdown bytes; retries of a candidate reuse its identity, sequence, and bytes. Successful completion means the destination durably accepted that candidate or already holds the same or a newer sequence. The returned sequence is the actual destination-held sequence at acknowledgment, not a promise it remains current. No TWG ingestion, Search visibility, Publication, or notification is implied. Generation failure creates no candidate and leaves any previous successful document intact. Once generation succeeds, a failed or uncertain delivery may leave a durable Exchange/candidate or an accepted destination document; an error is not a rollback guarantee. Repeating start is safe for the same Connection and Subject, but may generate a newer candidate if Jira content changed. Concurrent starts must not allocate conflicting sequences or replace newer destination content with older content. Errors expose only code and message, never source data, partial Workdown, credentials, or storage diagnostics.

params.name: connection
params.description: Local outbound Connection identifier. Ticket 20 recognizes only development-loopback in the development environment; it is not a caller-selected endpoint or installation identity.

params.name: issue
params.description: Source Jira issue key or ID, resolved as the authenticated caller. Stable document identity is not derived from a mutable issue key.

result.name: Accepted current document
result.description: A destination-acceptance acknowledgment, not a Publication receipt. Use connection and document with document.get; no separate Exchange or Publication ID is introduced.

methods.name: document.get
methods.summary: Read the latest retained Workdown at the destination
methods.description: Read-only. Authenticate a reader within the destination installation's site boundary. Source-site access, Project Admin authority, and a destination project or Epic are not required: shared content is unrestricted within that destination boundary under ADR 0001, never public internet content. Resolve the incoming Connection and document only within the trusted local installation, never from caller-supplied site identities or endpoints. The fixed development loopback may act as both outbound and incoming only in development. Require an active incoming Connection and a currently retained document; an unknown, wrong-direction, pending, revoked, or unavailable Connection yields Connection unavailable without state details. A missing or withdrawn document on an accessible active incoming Connection yields Document unavailable. Return the stored Workdown bytes and their actual stored sequence together from one consistent read. No Jira regeneration, historical version selection, source authorization check, TWG query, or ingestion acknowledgment is implied. A later sequence than the event or start acknowledgment is valid. Storage failure must never masquerade as a missing document. Lifecycle checks must fence reads against locally committed revocation; already-disclosed copies cannot be recalled. Errors expose only code and message, never document content or diagnostics.

params.description: Destination-local incoming Connection context, not a site URL.

methods.name: logs.list
methods.summary: List a bounded candidate page of governed installation-local log events.
methods.description: Requires a current human Jira global ADMINISTER check at the business boundary on every read, including continuations. Authenticated webtrigger credentials and trusted Forge-session invocation are supported; the verified human identity must match the Command principal. Native adapters supply trusted installation and principal context, never browser-asserted identity. Kind selects one partition of the Custom Entity event store. Filters combine with AND and are applied after reading at most limit candidates. Results are newest-first by canonical UTC CloudEvent time, then event ID descending for ties, using a time index; queries are eventually consistent and not a snapshot. The first call fixes effective retained-history time bounds; continuations preserve them. Coverage is Custom Entity events only after the implementation switch. No migration, backfill, or legacy KVS read fallback; earlier retained KVS audit events are outside this viewer. Empty results do not establish absence of pre-cutover activity. Empty pages can have a continuation. from is inclusive, to exclusive; require valid canonical UTC timestamps and from < to when both supplied. A supplied cursor is transient, query/installation-bound, authenticated, and expires after 15 minutes; repeat all effective query parameters. Never use it as authority. Cross-field event constraints and byte bounds are business validation obligations. No total count or complete reporting guarantee.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 20; maximum candidates scanned and returned, not a promise of matching count.

params.name: type
params.description: Exact CloudEvent type; must belong to the selected kind.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Transient opaque token returned by a previous identical query; not a durable bookmark.

DocumentId.description: Proposed encoding: the Subject's stable Jira source_id ARI, interpreted only within its Connection context. It survives issue-key changes. No separate Exchange ID. Internal storage/TWG key encoding must preserve this scoped identity without treating it as a raw storage key.

UpdateSequenceNumber.description: Positive JSON safe integer, monotonically increasing per Connection/document. Unchanged canonical bytes reuse the sequence; retries reuse bytes and sequence. Gaps are allowed. Not a timestamp or historical-version selector. Exhaustion must fail without wrapping.

RetryFailureKind.description: Safe category only; authorization/validation are permanent. No raw error or credential.

oneOf.description: UTC ISO 8601 timestamp with milliseconds; must also be a real calendar instant.

RetryStageStatus.description: Last recorded local progress, not remote truth or a live-worker claim. attempts is an observed 0–4 policy ordinal, not total network calls. Acknowledged last success survives failure. No enqueue-gap/retention recovery. Legacy unknowns stay null. Invariants and retry policy: specs/workdown-retries.md.

x-notifications.name: publication.published
x-notifications.summary: A Publication occurred at the destination
x-notifications.description: Emitted destination-locally once, after destination acceptance and acknowledged TWG ingestion of an update. Not emitted for unchanged content, stale or duplicate receipts, rejected ingestion, or an update superseded before acknowledgment is recorded. Carries identity only: no Workdown content, source data, or TWG diagnostics. Consumers retrieve the latest content with document.get, which may return a later sequence than the event's; that is valid. Delivery is at-least-once; consumers deduplicate on connection, document and updateSequenceNumber. This is a JSON-RPC 2.0 notification (method publication.published, params carrying this payload, no id), not a Forge App Event or a native Automation Flows trigger; no such trigger is claimed. It implies neither Search visibility nor webhook delivery.
